text:

He ran from the tent to meet them, bowed to the ground and begged them not to pass by. "Let a little water be brought so you can wash your feet and rest under the tree," he said, "and I will fetch a bite of bread so you can refresh yourselves."

text:

Ramesses was nearly destroyed in an ambush and fought his way out. Both kings claimed victory, and Ramesses covered temple walls with his version. text:

But, the book of Judges says, God told him the army was too large: if they won, Israel would boast that it had saved itself.

location: En Gedi, near the Dead Sea (modern Israel)
text:

On the way, Saul went alone into a cave to relieve himself. He did not know that David and his men were hiding deep in the same cave.

text:

text:

Its owner, the one eyed giant Polyphemus, came home with his flocks, rolled an enormous stone across the entrance, and ate two of the men for supper. text:

text:
Around 594 BC Athens was close to civil war. Poor farmers were sinking into debt and many had been enslaved for it, while the wealthy held the land and power. The Athenians gave Solon, a poet and merchant trusted by both sides, special authority to reform the city.

text:

The lapdog lived in the house. He knew clever tricks, sat on his master's knee, and whenever the master dined out, he came home with a treat for his dog.

text:
A fisherman who lived on what his nets brought in had a bad day. After hours of work he pulled in his net and found only one fish in it, and a very small one at that.

The little fish gasped and flapped and begged for its life. What use was it to him? It was hardly a mouthful. It was not yet grown. text:

text:

title: Wheelwright Pian and Duke Huan
text:
Duke Huan was reading a book up in his hall, while below, in the courtyard, a wheelwright named Pian was chiseling a wheel. Pian put down his tools, went up the steps and asked the duke what he was reading.

"The words of the sages," said the duke. "Are the sages still alive?" asked Pian. "They are dead." "Then what you are reading is only the dregs of the ancients."

The duke was angry. How dare a wheelwright comment on his reading? "If you can explain yourself, well and good. If not, you die."

text:
